ca_zsa_zsa_gabor_memorial_boulder.blurb: One large boulder of dark grey stone in the North Hollywood section of the OZ area, in the Pinto Basin of Joshua Tree National Park. It carries eight short routes: four sport, three trad and one top-rope. Seven of them fall at 5.9 or in the 5.10 range, with a single 5.11. The boulder stays out of sight for most of the walk and only appears when you are nearly at its base. Its lower elevation and sheltered position make it a workable choice on a cold, windy day when higher spots in the park are unpleasant.
ca_zsa_zsa_gabor_memorial_boulder.approach: Plan on roughly 45 to 60 minutes of easy walking up a sandy wash, which opens into a broad valley. Turn north toward the dark boulders at the foot of the rocky hillside.

ca_tinka_dome.blurb: A dome in the Eldorado National Forest, up the valley from Bear River Reservoir off Highway 88. It faces southeast, so the face is sunny. There are eight routes mixing sport, trad and top-rope: two at 5.5, two at 5.7, two at 5.8, then one 5.10 top-rope and one 5.11. That spread suits climbers building up on moderate leads, with a couple of harder lines for later. Views from the top of the dome are a draw. In winter it can still be reached with snowshoes when the snow lies deep.

ca_skyy_slab.blurb: A small formation on the back side of Coyote Crag in the Central Pinnacles of Holcomb Valley, San Bernardino Mountains, at about 7,500 ft. It faces northwest. Eight routes mix sport, trad and a single top-rope, and nearly all of them are moderate: three at 5.5, then one each at 5.6, 5.7, 5.8, 5.9 and 5.10. The slab sits close to the Tombstone Pit and around the corner from Mad Cow Wall, so it pairs easily with neighbouring crags. From the northern lot, the crags in this part of the Pinnacles are a 5 to 10 minute walk.

ca_swing_dance_boulder.blurb: A large boulder at about 8,400 ft in the Shangri-La Valley, on the Tramway side of the San Jacinto Mountains, and the first big rock you meet on the way into the Dance Floor area. It has eight problems from V1 up to V7: two at V1, one V2, three at V4 and two at V7. Faces range from gently overhanging and slabby to a short, steep wall, so there is something for most levels before the top-end lines. The Dance Floor sits on fairly level ground, with the walk-in crossing a seasonal stream.

ca_roadside_boulder_11.blurb: A single boulder beside West Camino Cielo in the hills above Santa Barbara, at about 2,500 ft, with no approach walk at all. It has eight problems from V0 to V6, concentrated in the middle: three at V2, two at V4, one each at V0, V3 and V6. Some of the lines are a little chossy. A good stop when you only want a short session or a warm-up near the road.

ca_right_side_upper_tier.blurb: The upper section of the right wall at Mayhem Cove, in Eagle Creek Canyon on Lake Tahoe's West Shore, at roughly 6,850 ft. All eight routes are sport climbs on granite, running from 5.10a to 5.12b: three in the 5.10 range, two at 5.11 and three at 5.12. The cove as a whole is steep to overhanging and heavily featured, and spring through fall is the usual window. A short trail climbs from the right wall and reaches the first route within a couple of minutes.
